{"verdict":"SUPPORTED","rationale":"The policy permits meals of $50 or less offered by a third party at a business meeting, with a cap of 4 per vendor per calendar year, matching the response."}

{"verdict":"SUPPORTED","rationale":"The response correctly states the over-$50 reporting requirement to the supervisor and Institutional Advancement Office, and accurately notes the policy does not say reported gifts may be kept; a $300 watch exceeds $50."}

{"verdict":"SUPPORTED","rationale":"The policy allows goodwill gifts from visiting officials, and gifts over $100 become University property to be discussed with the department head; a gift under $100 stays personal. The response matches this."}

{"verdict":"UNSUPPORTED","rationale":"The policy says nominal gifts are under $50, but also bars any gift that is intended to or could be construed as influencing a business decision. The response gives unconditional permission and ignores that condition."}

{"verdict":"SUPPORTED","rationale":"Response accurately describes the two exceptions in the text (group meals/beverages at professional events; purchases at public prices), hedges on concert tickets, and refers the employee to HR/compliance without asserting unsupported rules."}

{"verdict":"SUPPORTED","rationale":"Policy bars accepting personal gifts from current or potential vendors, which covers vendors bidding on a contract; declining is consistent. Mention of Penn is minor and not contradicted."}

{"verdict":"SUPPORTED","rationale":"Policy permits unsolicited gifts under $50 not intended to influence official action, placed in a common department area for sharing; a $20 token shared with the team fits. 'Tokens' wording is minor."}

The phone number is listed as a policy contact, but calling it the HR office is also unsupported."}

{"verdict":"UNSUPPORTED","rationale":"Policy says gifts over $100 become University property and should be discussed with the department head, but does not say to turn them over to the head; also the stated purpose, to \"maintain the appearance of a conflict of interest,\" is wrong, since the policy aims to avoid it."}

{"verdict":"UNSUPPORTED","rationale":"Policy says gifts over $50 should be reported, but only prohibits gifts intended to or construed as influencing business decisions. Saying the employee should not keep the watch regardless is unsupported, as is the unseen 'No' framing."}

{"verdict":"SUPPORTED","rationale":"The policy states it does not prohibit accepting meals or beverages from suppliers when offered to a large group at a professional event or meeting, matching the response's hedged answer."}

{"verdict":"UNSUPPORTED","rationale":"The policy says scarce tickets \"may not be accepted\" and only addresses buying thank-you tickets at face value; it does not say gifts for official actions are flatly barred for tickets, nor mention vendors or conflicts of interest."}
{"verdict":"UNSUPPORTED","rationale":"The policy sets no dollar threshold and does not mention umbrellas; claiming a $25 umbrella exceeds the 'typical nominal value' is not supported by the text."}

{"verdict":"UNSUPPORTED","rationale":"The policy says gift cards must be immediately returned to the donor; it mentions no Gifts and Prizes Reporting Form or Accounts Payable submission, and submitting the card contradicts the return requirement."}

{"verdict":"UNSUPPORTED","rationale":"The policy only requires prior written dean/vice president approval for supplier-paid trips; it says nothing about equipment inspection, evaluating goods or sites, or University reimbursement for such trips."}

{"verdict":"UNSUPPORTED","rationale":"The policy text says nothing about tickets, trips, or gift amounts, and it allows exceptions approved by the President or designee, so the claim of no exceptions is contradicted."}

{"verdict":"UNSUPPORTED","rationale":"The policy sets the threshold at $50, not $25; items of $50 or less are not described as a general $25 allowance, so the response misstates the figure."}

{"verdict":"UNSUPPORTED","rationale":"The policy bars additional gifts only from contributors to the class gift; a non-contributing parent's $25 spa certificate is not barred by the text, so the blanket 'no' is unsupported."}

{"verdict":"UNSUPPORTED","rationale":"The policy text never says gifts cannot influence supplier selection, never bars retention \"under no circumstances,\" and never requires reporting to Procurement Services; it allows nominal-value items."}

{"verdict":"SUPPORTED","rationale":"The policy states cash gifts from patients or their families are not permitted, which matches the response's statement that the employee cannot accept the cash gift."}

{"verdict":"SUPPORTED","rationale":"The policy states it does not prohibit employees from buying goods for personal use when paying consideration equal to the general public; the laptop example is consistent with this."}

{"verdict":"UNSUPPORTED","rationale":"The policy text cuts off before listing the conditions in the general prohibition, so it doesn't support that contractors' gifts are barred or that a $20 gift is impermissible; the response's reading of the prohibition is also circular."}

{"verdict":"SUPPORTED","rationale":"Policy states a teacher receiving a class gift may not knowingly accept additional gifts from participating parents or students, and class gifts up to $150 are allowed, matching the response."}

{"verdict":"UNSUPPORTED","rationale":"The policy states that gift cards and cash equivalents are not permitted at all, so saying it doesn't specify a maximum for gift cards misleadingly implies they might be allowed."}

{"verdict":"UNSUPPORTED","rationale":"The exception requires meals to be occasional and non-repetitive; a monthly meal from the same vendor is repetitive, and the response wrongly treats regularity as qualifying."}

{"verdict":"SUPPORTED","rationale":"Policy permits nominal gifts in kind under $50, and chocolates under $50 fit this; the response's claim is consistent with the policy text."}
